rows.title: The staging queue held 599 pending records and was never read. Measured: it is TWO populations sharing one counter — 24 machine-collected SP-API/Ads rows (trust 85, ~5/day, ongoing) and 575 knowledge records (573 of them trust 50-69, batch-imported over 4 days in July, static since). 15 of the 24 have NO counterpart in core/, including every `ads_campaigns` record (never promoted) and all of today's collection
rows.status: implemented v1 (ADR-0163). `promote --source A,B` promotes every pending record from those sources; batch DEFAULTS TO DRY RUN (a mistyped flag must not promote hundreds into a delete-free store, ADR-0005) while the single-id form keeps REFUSED+exit 2. `--source` selects, never flushes; a "promote everything" verb is deliberately absent. The gate is untouched: --approve still required, approved_by still HUMAN_OWNER (ADR-0004) — only the BATCH SIZE of one approval changed. TWO SUSPICIONS CHECKED AND DROPPED: `promote` does mark the staging copy, so the 9 core-and-staging overlaps are not a marking bug (staged_at is later than promoted_at in each — they are later re-collections carrying 0-2 extra late-arriving order rows); and there are ZERO duplicate contents across all 599, so no dedup shortcut exists. 7 tests; 1366 total green

rows.title: The 575 knowledge records need a promotion criterion; source-batching is the wrong instrument
rows.status: **criterion set** (ADR-0164). Three candidates measured and two eliminated by evidence. TRUST FLOOR IS IMPOSSIBLE, structurally: the flat `scores.trust` is a per-TYPE constant (all 274 transcripts exactly 60, all 101 `number` exactly 55), and the per-record curation trust (ADR-0104, 283 records) lands 22.0-32.3 with NONE above 40 because seven of ten components are flat zero — historical_accuracy (weight 15), experiment_results, verification_status, human_validation, ai_agreement, contradiction_level, consensus. Those move only when a claim is validated or tested, i.e. by the review itself, so a threshold is circular and re-running curation cannot lift the ceiling. `curated-active` (273) is not an endorsement either — it means "not duplicate/superseded/conflict". CRITERION IS CONTACT, NOT SCORE: a claim becomes promotable when a validation component leaves zero, i.e. when checked against something ODIN measured (now possible — ACOS 8.2%, ROAS 12.16, margin 31.4%, refunds 9.22% over 48 SKUs). Today it admits ZERO records, which is the honest answer: the queue was never unread, it is correctly parked awaiting a validation mechanism that does not exist. 6 tests; 1371 total green

rows.title: 274 transcripts closed as `source-material` — consumed input, not knowledge. The extraction agent (ADR-0032) already produced 301 claims from them and 73 name their source transcript in provenance; promoting a raw YouTube caption would make it citable as fact
rows.status: done (ADR-0164). New `stage-mark --type <t> --as <status> [--approve]`: dry-run by default, appends a new version so the `pending` state stays readable (ADR-0005), and REFUSES `--as promoted` by name because it writes a status and not the Core — granting promotion there would bypass the owner's gate (ADR-0004). Queue 577 -> 303. No automation built for future transcripts: they arrived in 4 batch days in July and none since, so an on-arrival rule would be speculation

rows.title: Build the validation mechanism ADR-0164's criterion depends on
rows.status: implemented v1 (ADR-0165). THREE MECHANISMS DIED ON EVIDENCE FIRST: deterministic semantic agreement is unavailable (claims are free-form Turkish prose, `content` holds only claim+evidence_quote, and the existing `consensus` uses `SequenceMatcher.ratio()` on normalised text — near-duplicate detection that found exactly ONE pair across 283 records); topic-level agreement would fabricate confidence (`tag_topic` proves five creators discussed bidding, not that they agreed); the model path is measured-unreliable (3 successful calls vs 12 errors, no price table). THE ACTUAL BLOCKER WAS AN UNWIRED INPUT: `claim_trust()` passes only source_reliability/evidence_quality/freshness/consensus and NEVER human_validation or verification_status, so an owner ruling would have changed nothing — reachable max 50, ~27 at real values, exactly the measured 22.0-32.3 band. New `owner_verdict()` writes both components and rescores through the SAME TrustScorer (no second score). `refuted` -> status `obsolete` (terminal) but verification_status still rises: "checked and wrong" is knowledge, and treating it as unknown discards the work. Reason mandatory (ADR-0131). New `claims [--match\
rows.closed_by: --topic]` PULLS claims with evidence quote — 301 records are not a reading list. Append-only via annotate (ADR-0005). Live: `claims --match acos` surfaces "önerilen ACOS hedefi %25" against a measured 8.2%. 6 tests; 1377 total green

rows.title: The outcome loop: a ruled claim still could not be cited, so `experiment_results` (10) and `historical_accuracy` (15) could never move
rows.status: **half fixed** (ADR-0166). Root cause was NOT decay: `publish_year` reads the year from claim TEXT, so only 8 of 281 claims had one and 273 took a flat unknown-year default of 50 — what separated a citable claim from an uncitable one was whether its sentence contained a four-digit number. Decay rate and unknown-year default now depend on the claim's KIND: evergreen (`method`) 5/year and 85 when undated, perishable 15/year and 40 — the default FELL for figures nobody can date and rose only where time is weakly informative. With a supported verdict, claims clearing CITABLE_MIN go **8 -> 124**; WITHOUT a verdict **0 of 283** clear it, pinned by a test, because freshness alone opening the gate would restore the defect in a new form. REMAINING HALF STILL OPEN: experiment_results and historical_accuracy are zero for every claim and moving them means attributing an outcome to a claim without separating it from everything else that changed in the same period — manufacturing causality. Council has NOT reviewed ADR-0166's policy values (MCP unavailable); question pack ready in ER-0037-MECLIS-SORUSU.md

rows.title: R-006 rows rendered with SHIFTED COLUMNS when their prose held an UNESCAPED pipe: the `status` cell showed a mid-sentence fragment and the ADR cell showed whatever followed. Separately, BR-0015 was missing its ADR cell entirely
rows.status: fixed (8 rows escaped + BR-0015's cell added). THE FIRST ATTEMPT MADE IT WORSE and was reverted: it counted every pipe character, so rows whose pipes were ALREADY escaped were double-escaped into a literal backslash — the same failure class this session kept finding, a check measuring the wrong thing and producing confident wrong action. The rerun splits on UNESCAPED pipes only and asserts that unescaping the output reproduces the input byte for byte; that assertion fired on the first run and stopped the write. `validate_docs` still does not check column counts — a gate is cheap but the 11 remaining hits are a legitimate 4-column table, so it needs a row-scoped rule rather than a global one

Measured: text 8, origin_path 56, combined 62; across the 2 claims where both signals fired they AGREED, so coverage widened without a conflict to arbitrate. With a supported verdict, claims clearing CITABLE_MIN go 124 -> 143; unruled claims clearing it stays 0. Not an intended effect; recorded because an unexplained count shift is discovered late. rows.title: **Freshness classification will need redesigning when a second knowledge family arrives.** Today `EVERGREEN_TYPES` has ONE member and the evergreen/perishable split maps cleanly onto `type`, because the whole corpus is creator videos about Amazon selling (281 claims: method/number/fact/note). A second family — regulation, API behaviour, a dated standard, a scientific finding — will not split on `type` alone: an API-behaviour claim decays on the vendor's release cadence, a regulation on its effective date, neither on a per-year percentage. When that arrives the classification must be reconsidered as a whole rather than extended by another row
rows.status: **open BY DESIGN, deliberately NOT implemented.** Owner ruling 2026-08-01: an ER is an architectural note about a future trigger, not today's code; a policy engine built now would be flexibility written against data ODIN does not have (the same class as the refused `ai_queue` channel and `universeId`). What WAS built is the smaller thing the owner asked for: `FreshnessClassifier` (ADR-0168) isolates the one decision and returns the rule that fired, so the redesign has a single place to happen. Trigger to reopen: the first claim whose `type` is not in (method, number, fact, note, observation)

rows.title: **Outcome learning must publish EVIDENCE STRENGTH, never a truth verdict.** ODIN should not say "this claim is true" but "evidence that acting on this claim succeeded: 68%", with Claim -> Recommendation -> Observed Outcome -> Alternative Explanations -> Confidence and the alternatives as a first-class field. Owner specified the target shape 2026-08-01: a Claim Assessment carrying evidence_strength, historical_success, missing_information, alternative_explanations, uncertainty, confidence, confidence_reason
rows.status: open — design recorded, NOT implemented (needs its own ADR + council round). WHY THIS DISSOLVES THE BLOCKER: attributing an outcome to a claim manufactures causality, but publishing evidence strength WITH the unexcluded alternatives does not — it states what is known and what is not. **SIX OF THE SEVEN FIELDS ALREADY HAVE CANONICAL ODIN NAMES and must reuse them, or ODIN ends up with two vocabularies for one concept (the drift ADR-0129 and ADR-0143 both fought):** evidence_strength (20,+1), historical_success (15,+1) and missing_information (5,**-1**, i.e. it LOWERS confidence as it rises — the natural home for unexcluded alternatives) are in `trust.CONFIDENCE_COMPONENTS` and REQUIRED by `decision-record.schema.json`; `alternative_explanations` is `flip_conditions`, already mandatory in `decision.py:76`; `uncertainty` is ADR-0085's `limitations`. Only **confidence_reason** is genuinely new, and it is the field that answers "why 72?" rather than only "72". So this is applying the decision layer's confidence discipline to claims, not inventing a scoring system. **OWNER RULING 2026-08-01 — build the envelope WITH ER-0040, not before it** (BR-0023): an envelope with no consumer is the same abstraction-without-data this session refused three times. **DECISION TRACE is part of the target**: explainability must answer HOW, not only WHY — `Claim -> Evidence -> Classifier -> Decay Rule -> Confidence Components -> Limitations -> Flip Conditions -> Confidence -> Confidence Reason -> Decision Trace`, reading like "this claim is a method so the evergreen rule fired; 2026 came from origin_path; missing_information subtracted 5; evidence_strength added 20; final confidence 82". TWO STEPS ALREADY EXIST and were not built for this: `decay_rule` (ADR-0168) records which classifier rule fired, and `measured`/`ceiling` (ADR-0169) record what was looked at and what was reachable. The trace is accumulating from the components rather than needing to be invented. **COUNCIL ROUND RUN 2026-08-01 (gavadolar 2/2, yazilimcilar 4/4) — v1 IS SMALLER THAN PROPOSED.** gavadolar unanimous on all five: ER-0040 IS the ADR-0085 implementation (not a new trust system), ER-0040 BEFORE ER-0037 (explainability is solvable with today's data, causality needs new data and time), ER-0040 v1 closes in one sprint. yazilimcilar 4/4 on reduction: `unmeasured`, `coverage`, `ceiling` and `confidence_state` are ALL DERIVABLE from `measured` plus the weight table and must NOT be persisted — compute them at read time. Only `measured` is irreducible (it is what distinguishes a measured 0.0 from an absent one). **terra found a defect in the proposed envelope nobody else caught: `"confidence": 82` alongside `TrustScorer`'s `trust: 30.5` creates TWO confidence numbers for one claim** — the envelope's confidence must BE the trust score, not a second one. terra also argues the human-readable reason should be DERIVED deterministically from `measured` + config rather than stored as prose ("3/9 components have data; the unmeasured ones cap the score at 50"), which keeps it from going stale and needs no LLM. SPLIT RECORDED: Qwen says `trace` and `confidence_reason` do NOT overlap (machine vs human question); terra, DeepSeek and Gemini-Flash say they do. Not resolved here

rows.title: **ADR-0085 (Explainability Envelope) is an accepted decision with ZERO implementation.** It mandates that any section marked `generatedBy: ai` carry an envelope with `model`, `evidenceRefs`, `confidence`, `limitations` and `humanOverride`, enforced structurally by a section schema (validation rules V-005/V-006). Measured 2026-08-01: `grep -rn explainability odin/*.py` returns nothing and no envelope schema file exists
rows.status: open. Found while mapping ER-0040's proposed Claim Assessment onto existing vocabulary — the owner's `uncertainty` field is this ADR's `limitations`, and its `confidence` + `evidenceRefs` are the same envelope. Implementing ER-0040 for claims would satisfy a mandate that has been unenforced since ADR-0085 was accepted; doing it under a NEW name would leave the mandate unmet AND create a second vocabulary. Whichever is built first should be built as the envelope

rows.title: `TrustScorer.score()` read components with `.get(name, 0.0)`, so a component nobody supplied entered the breakdown as a measured 0. Every claim published `historical_accuracy: 0.0` — reading as "we checked its track record and it has none" when the truth is "nothing was ever measured". Same defect class as ADR-0156's `ai_spend: 0.0` over three real calls
rows.status: fixed (ADR-0169). Composite arithmetic UNCHANGED and pinned by a test — an unmeasured component still contributes nothing, because nothing was measured; only the reporting changed. Score now ships `measured`, `unmeasured`, `coverage` ("3/9") and `ceiling` (sum of supplied weights). Today's claims read coverage 3/9 ceiling 50.0; with an owner verdict, 5/9 and 60.0 — the numbers ADR-0164 had to derive by hand are now stated by the thing that produced them. `breakdown` keeps its numeric shape: turning absent values into `None` would break every consumer and force two types on each caller, so the distinction lives in the new fields. Owner proposed the value `unknown`/`not_measured`; right about the fact, wrong about the mechanism — a string in a weighted sum either raises or is coerced back to zero somewhere less visible. 4 tests; 1391 total green

rows.title: `coverage: "3/9"` and `ceiling: 50.0` are enough for a reader who knows the weight table, but a screen or another agent would each re-derive the same judgement and drift apart doing it
rows.status: implemented v1 (ADR-0170). `confidence_state` ships with every score: `measured` (all supplied) / `partial` (ceiling >= 40) / `insufficient` (0 < ceiling < 40, can NEVER be citable whatever the values) / `unavailable` (nothing measured). Follows the existing `TRUST_BANDS` pattern of labelling a number rather than making consumers interpret it. THE BOUNDARY IS NOT A NEW NUMBER: 40 is already `TRUST_BANDS`' `provisional` line and the value `decision.CITABLE_MIN` enforces, and a test asserts the two stay equal so they cannot drift silently. State is about COVERAGE not value — a perfect 100 on one component reads `insufficient`, pinned by a test, because that is the exact confusion the field prevents. OWNER'S THRESHOLDS ADJUSTED WITH A REASON: the proposal keyed states off the count (9/9, 6/9, 3/9); weight is the honest basis since the nine components carry different weights (3-of-9 by count is 50-of-100 by weight for a claim) and weight determines what the score can reach — the count still ships as `coverage`. Today's claims read `partial`; nothing reads `measured`, correctly. 3 tests; 1394 total green

rows.title: **Derived trust fields are PERSISTED and have already drifted from the code that derives them.** `curate` and `owner_verdict` write the whole `TrustScorer.score()` dict into each claim's `curation.trust` block. Measured 2026-08-01 across all 283 staged claims: 283/283 carry `coverage` and `ceiling` (ADR-0169 fields) and **283/283 are MISSING `confidence_state`** (ADR-0170), because curation has not run since that field was added. A consumer reading stored records cannot tell which code version produced what
rows.status: open. This is exactly the failure yazilimcilar 4/4 predicted in the ER-0040 round — a value computed from other values, frozen in storage, diverges from its function. NOT "FIXED" BY RE-RUNNING CURATION: that would re-freeze at today's version and reproduce the same drift on the next change. The fix is to stop persisting what can be derived, which is ER-0040's design decision and belongs to that ADR.
